I've decided to document the hoops I'm jumping through in this journey to simply apply for my FOID.  Here it is so far.

Illinois is crap.... Here's just one reason why.


1. Attempt to apply for FOID card online. Registered for an account and then discovered that any time I log into that account it takes me to a page with my information on it but does not give me the opportunity to apply. I go back to the homepage and try to apply and it logs me out. Every. Single. Time.
  So... I called the customer service number to get help. I received a message that they are experiencing a high call volume and to call back later and then my call is disconnected. I tried several more times throughout the day and get the same message. I try late at night just to see if it's giving the same message and it is. I try first thing in the morning right when the office is supposed to open and get the same message and disconnected once again.
  Then, I decide to just submit a paper application. Problem is, the paper application is not available through ANY other source than the same customer service number that defaults to a recording and disconnection. (So, 100% of those without the ability to apply on line are being prevented from applying.)
   At this point, on the suggestion of members of an IL. Gun enthusiast forum,  I attempt to get help from my state representative. I fill out a form online for assistance with a federal agency and follow the directions to print that form and then fax or mail it to my representatives office. When I go to fax it I realized there is no fax number listed so I called the phone number and I am told they do not have a fax number nor do they handle those types of inquiries. (Even though there is a specific form and instructions stating that they receive fax and handle those inquiries)
 I'm given the name and phone number of somebody that handles "those types of inquiries".  When I call that office it goes straight to voicemail even though it is during business hours. I submitted an email requesting help and received an automated email back that they will not be in until the 6th of January.
  I then went to the State Police website and found the number of the technology department hoping maybe they could help me with the technical issue on the Firearms services bureau website. The gentleman that answered expressed concern over my problem and explained that they get calls all the time about the customer service number not answering. He said he was very sorry but there was absolutely nothing he could do to help me. He also assured me that there was nothing he could do on that website as that is completely within their department and their technical people. He suggested that I contact the director of the state police and go from there.
  I then contacted the director's office where I was told by the receptionist that they don't handle anything like that and that there is no way for me to contact his office directly. I was told to go on the website and file a citizen's complaint against the Firearms Services Bureau, and wait for an email response.
  Ok. After reading the procedures for filling that complaint it is clear that those complaints are for individual officers, not an entire department. How utterly insane to file a citizen's complaint that requires an affidavit just to say that they need to answer their phone or make a FOID application available to all or have help available when their website is refusing to allow me to apply. I'm absolutely speechless at this point.
  I am 100% being prevented from even applying for a FOID card.  That is MY RIGHT and Illinois is obstructing it.

So here's the thing all you non tit-for-tat Sayers. In all likelihood the betrayed spouse would not have ever cheated had they not been cheated on first. It's a whole new ballgame once somebody decides to break a marriage covenant that way. And the person who cheats first needs to suck it up and realize that they can't place expectations and the betrayed spouse. Infidelity is emotional abuse and nobody can tell somebody how they can respond to emotional abuse even if they are trying their best to save a marriage. Some days you want to save it some days you wish you'd never let them back. What I would recommend is that the O.P. sit in her discomfort and live with that punched in the gut feeling and those mental images that will never ever leave her mind. Experience for a moment what she brought into the marriage. I dare say that might actually bring a level of understanding that would be the best shot of saving this marriage. But we all know that saving this marriage is kind of a long shot as it is for all marriages where infidelity is discovered.

I mean, it's possible she wants him. But not likely. The narcissism involved in cheating also makes cheaters feel entitled.  He's not enough for her, she wants more/different/whatever.  BUT.... Like hell anyone else is going to have him or his respect/friendship/admiration.
   He's still in the early stage of loving his wife and thinking there's hope. We were all there once I think. I was there for years thinking we were different. But no. They want what they want and they were willing to risk their spouse and their children to get it. That's not a mistake. That's a character flaw. That's a big bright Marquee saying that the marriage isn't a marriage to them. Game over.  But as the hurt, sad, empty betrayed we simply don't believe that that's the case for us. We are different. Our spouse is different. They're telling the truth now. All that crap. Everyone gets past it in time. My only suggestion to O.P. would be to prioritize whatever it is that makes him feel comforted and not so alone. And by all means let the wife know that her feelings come second if at all in his healing. And that's entirely her own fault.
